name: Shellac
label: Touch and Go
lede: The most famous recording engineer in rock spent 32 years in a trio that took questions mid-set, gave its second album away to 779 named friends, and put out its last record ten days after he died.

eras.title: A drummer from the 7th Street Entry
eras.text: After Big Black and Rapeman, Steve Albini was a working engineer with no band. A Minneapolis drummer he'd met years earlier and a Boston bassist who moved to Chicago for a studio job turned a few jam sessions into a trio that never changed its line-up.

years.h: Steve Albini and Todd Trainer start jamming in Minneapolis
years.p: [[Todd Trainer|6c123659-4d26-487f-b156-6b56ffa2bc4c]] of [[Rifle Sport|54f70716-5cef-43e0-99c1-d91b5bd518b4]] and [[Breaking Circus|5f92a6ee-44ef-4eef-8b5b-1bd359b32fd4]] had introduced himself to Steve Albini at the first [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]] show at Minneapolis's 7th Street Entry. Years later, on trips to Minneapolis to rehearse with Flour, Albini started playing with him.
years.xp: Albini told The Wire the two began putting together music that seemed like it was actually a band. Trainer was also a one-man band as [[Brick Layer Cake|0e15affb-9c59-4c63-99f0-72e44b92c315]], playing and singing everything himself.

years.h: Shellac tries Naked Raygun's Camilo Gonzalez on bass
years.p: Chicago punk veteran Camilo Gonzalez of [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]] rehearses with Steve Albini and Todd Trainer and plays on Shellac's first single. Albini said later they could tell it wasn't going to be the band.

years.h: Bob Weston leaves Boston for Albini's studio, and joins Shellac
years.p: Albini had recorded the last [[Volcano Suns|4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc]] album, and bassist [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]] moved to Chicago to work at Albini's home studio. Once Weston played with Albini and Trainer, Albini said, it felt like a complete band.
years.xp: Weston told The Wire that joining wasn't a foregone conclusion when he moved. Shellac's first gigs were unannounced sets at a Chicago tavern where a friend worked.

years.h: Steve Albini records Nirvana's In Utero for a flat fee
years.p: Shellac's guitarist engineers [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s third album and, as always, takes a flat fee and no royalties. He called himself a recording engineer, never a producer.
years.xp: Before the sessions Albini wrote the band a letter setting out how he worked, including his preference for mixing what he recorded. Wikipedia notes his refusal of royalties meant little passive income even from later hits like Bush's Razorblade Suitcase.

years.h: Shellac's first singles: The Rude Gesture and Uranus
years.p: Touch and Go releases The Rude Gesture: A Pictorial History and Uranus, both 7" singles. Uranus carries Wingwalker, for which the band acts out airplane moves on stage.
years.xp: Albini told The Quietus the band decided from the start not to do any promotion. Wingwalker stayed in the set for decades, and Albini improvised its spoken part differently every night.

years.h: Shellac's first real tour starts in Japan, not America
years.p: Shellac tours Japan, Australia and New Zealand before playing almost anywhere in the US. A Tokyo show on November 21, 1993 becomes the Live in Tokyo CD on Japan's NUX Organization.
years.xp: Bob Weston told The Wire the thinking was simple: Albini was famous, so Shellac wouldn't be allowed to learn how to be a band on an American stage. Their only US show before that tour was an Augenblick gig.

years.h: Albini's The Problem with Music runs in The Baffler
years.p: Steve Albini's essay in The Baffler No. 5 walks through a hypothetical $250,000 major-label deal in which each band member ends up with $4,031.25.
years.xp: In the same piece he attacked [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]]'s move to Geffen. Shellac later ran without advances, managers or booking agents.

eras.title: Second only to Oasis
eras.text: Shellac's debut album was a hit by indie standards, and the band did nothing to push it. The next record was pressed for 779 named friends and never sold at all.

years.h: The Bird Is the Most Popular Finger on Drag City
years.p: Shellac's third single comes out on Chicago's Drag City rather than Touch and Go.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: At Action Park
years.h: At Action Park, Shellac's debut album on Touch and Go
years.p: Recorded at Southern in London and Black Box in France, At Action Park reaches No. 2 on the UK indie chart, Albini recalled, stuck behind Oasis.
years.xp:
Albini's sound came from copper picks, Travis Bean aluminum-neck guitars and a Harmonic Percolator distortion pedal, with Weston's bass and Trainer's huge, spare drumming. The vinyl came out weeks before the CD because of manufacturing delays.

Albini told The Quietus he found Oasis trivial. Fact ranked At Action Park the 18th best album of the 1990s in 2012.

years.h: Steve Albini founds Electrical Audio in Chicago
years.p: Albini's recording business moves from his house toward Electrical Audio, a Chicago studio built to record bands live and cheaply. Shellac makes most of its records there.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the founding to 1995; the Chicago building on Belmont Avenue is often dated 1997. By his death Albini's day rate was $900, and he'd keep working unpaid if a band ran out of money.

years.h: The Futurist: a dance score pressed for 779 friends
years.p: Shellac's music for Montreal dance company La La La Human Steps is pressed in 779 copies and given away. Every recipient's name is printed on the sleeve, with their own name circled.
years.xp: The name list was there to stop anyone selling a copy. Albini told The Quietus used copies still went for around $500. Recorded in 1995, the 27-minute piece was never sold in shops.

eras.title: The long, slow, boring song
eras.text: Shellac's next two proper albums opened with a twelve-minute dirge and closed with a promise that the band had become meaner. Then a band that avoided festivals ended up running one at an English holiday camp.

years.h: Terraform opens with a twelve-minute slow song
years.p: Shellac's second commercial album starts with Didn't We Deserve a Look at You the Way You Really Are, which the band called The Long, Slow, Boring Song while writing it.
years.xp: Recorded between 1995 and December 1996. The cover uses space art by Chesley Bonestell. Albini told The Quietus the band was a very selfish enterprise: it made the records it wanted to hear.

years.h: 1000 Hurts, packaged like a box of Ampex tape
years.p: Shellac's third album comes in a sleeve modeled on an Ampex reel-to-reel tape box. The band's promo note warned it was more mean-spirited than the last, and that Todd sings.
years.xp:
The title plays on 1000 hertz, a calibration tone, and the album opens like an MRL test tape. Albini told The Quietus Canaveral paints JFK as a womanizer, and that listeners often misread Prayer to God as an endorsement.

Jehnny Beth of Savages said 1000 Hurts made her want to play bass.

yt: Shellac at ATP, Camber Sands, April 19, 2002
years.h: Shellac curates All Tomorrow's Parties at Camber Sands
years.p: The band that turned down festivals curates ATP at a Pontins holiday camp on the English coast. Wikipedia says [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]]'s turn as ATP curator had talked Albini into playing the festival in the first place.
years.xp: Albini later said ATP completely changed the festival game, with curated line-ups where everyone was treated well. Shellac took early slots so fans would go see other bands.

eras.title: Any questions?
eras.text: Shellac settled into a rhythm: an album every seven years, a yearly trip to Barcelona, and a show that stopped halfway so the crowd could shout questions and the band could shout back.

yt: Full set, Primavera Sound (Sala Apolo), Barcelona, 2017
years.h: Shellac becomes Primavera Sound's house band
years.p: Shellac plays Primavera Sound in Barcelona for the first time and comes back nearly every year after. In 2018 the festival sold merch reading Shellac and 249 More.

q: I did that so I wouldn't have to have ridiculous stage banter.
years.h: Shellac's mid-set Q&A: Bob Weston's cure for stage banter
years.p: At Shellac shows, Bob Weston would stop and take questions from the crowd. It started as a way to fill the gap while Steve Albini retuned after Song of the Minerals.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the answers as off-the-cuff and at times jocular. When fans asked to play the drums during the questions, Todd Trainer would hop off his stool and hand over his sticks, The Wire reported.

years.src: Wikipedia: Excellent Italian Greyhound · The Quietus
years.h: Excellent Italian Greyhound, named for Todd Trainer's dog
years.p: Shellac's first album in seven years is named for Todd Trainer's Italian greyhound, Uffizi, who is on the cover. It opens with The End of Radio, half improvised every time they play it.
years.xp: Genuine Lulabelle features uncredited voice work from Ken Nordine and clips of the Homestar Runner character Strong Bad. Spoke opens with a cover of a Rotosound Strings ad from The Who's The Who Sell Out. Mastered at Abbey Road.

years.cap: Bob Weston with Shellac at ATP, 2007
years.h: Shellac ends shows by taking Todd Trainer's drum kit apart
years.p: Shellac shows close with Steve Albini and Bob Weston dismantling Todd Trainer's drum kit while he keeps playing. Setlists were about half planned, half chosen on the spot, Albini said.

yt: Shellac at ATP curated by Shellac, Camber Sands, December 2, 2012
years.h: Shellac curates ATP again for its 20th anniversary
years.p: Ten years after its first turn, Shellac curates All Tomorrow's Parties at Camber Sands, with [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]], [[Mission of Burma|db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e]], The Ex, [[Neurosis|a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed]], Arcwelder and Oxbow on the bill.

eras.title: Surveyors and poker bracelets
eras.text: Shellac made one album in this stretch, about surveyors. Albini spent the rest of it telling the music business the internet had solved its problems, apologizing for his younger self, and winning at poker.

years.h: Dude Incredible: Shellac sings about surveyors
years.p: Shellac's fifth album runs a suite of songs about surveyors, and is the first time all three members sing in unison. It reaches No. 85 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: Albini told The Quietus that many early American patriots were surveyors with ground-level knowledge of the land. The chipboard sleeve carries two monkeys shot by Reuters photographer Anton Meres. It was mastered entirely in analog.

yt: Face the Music 2014 keynote: Steve Albini
years.h: Albini tells Face the Music the internet fixed his old complaint
years.p: In a keynote at Melbourne's Face the Music conference, Steve Albini calls the old label system wasteful and praises file-sharing for letting ignored music find listeners.

yt: The End of Radio, live at Primavera Sound, 2018
years.h: The End of Radio collects Shellac's John Peel sessions
years.p: Touch and Go releases Shellac's two sessions for BBC DJ [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]], from 1994 and 2004.

years.h: Steve Albini publicly regrets his old provocations
years.p: In a widely shared Twitter thread, Albini says much of what he said and did from a position of comfort and privilege was awful and that he regrets it.
years.xp: He wrote that he'd wrongly assumed misogyny and homophobia were solved problems, and regretted treating fascism as a joke. By 2023 he said he was embarrassed by Rapeman's name. [[Kim Deal|760e4df4-e851-46c8-b34d-afa2e9706831]] said the person he'd become could move her to tears.

years.h: Steve Albini wins his second World Series of Poker bracelet
years.p: Albini wins a $1,500 H.O.R.S.E. event for $196,089, four years after taking a $1,500 stud event for $105,629.

eras.title: Ten days
eras.text: Shellac announced its first album in a decade with no singles, no tour and no advance copies. Steve Albini died ten days before it came out, and the tributes came from the places the band had made its own.

q: Marketing, which is maybe my most hated thing on earth.
years.src: Wikipedia: To All Trains · The Wire
years.h: Shellac announces To All Trains and refuses to promote it
years.p: Shellac announces its first album in ten years for May 17 on Touch and Go, with no singles, no tour dates and no copies for critics.
years.xp: Bob Weston told The Wire the band had never let anyone hear a record before release day in 30 years. The album had been finished for a while, held up by Covid, interrupted tours and pressing-plant delays.

years.h: Steve Albini dies of a heart attack at 61
years.p: Steve Albini dies of a heart attack at his home in Chicago on May 7, 2024. Shellac's line-up had not changed in 32 years.
years.xp:
That day, The Wire issue with Shellac on the cover went on sale. Emily Pothast had interviewed all three members on April 15, in what she called the band's final long-form interview.

[[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]] dedicated My Hero to him, and [[Joanna Newsom|cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c]] played Cosmia in his memory.

years.src: The Wire · Wikipedia: To All Trains
years.h: To All Trains comes out ten days after Albini's death
years.p: Shellac's final album, recorded at Electrical Audio between 2017 and 2022, is named for words Steve Albini saw on an archway at Chicago's Union Station.
years.xp:
Bob Weston shot the archway for the cover; his iPhone photo of himself taking it went on the back. Inside are photos of scrapper trucks, one per member, for the song Scrappers.

It reached No. 12 in Scotland and No. 44 in Germany. AllMusic's Mark Deming said it was impossible to hear without grief.

years.h: Primavera Sound plays To All Trains in Shellac's slot
years.p: Primavera Sound fills Shellac's scheduled set with a listening party for To All Trains and renames a stage the Steve Albini stage.

years.h: Chicago unveils Steve Albini Way outside Electrical Audio
years.p: The block of Belmont Avenue at Rockwell, where Electrical Audio stands, becomes Steve Albini Way. [[Kim Deal|760e4df4-e851-46c8-b34d-afa2e9706831]] and Albini's widow, Heather Whinna, speak at the unveiling.
years.xp: At the afterparty inside the studio, [[Jeff Tweedy|63287966-6021-474a-ba76-edc37a5f1b7c]], Fred Armisen and [[The Mekons|66d2169c-dea5-46d3-b4cb-52ed87b24ab0]]' Jon Langford and Sally Timms played as the Electrical Adjacents.
